title: 734. Minimum Window Subsequence

examples.explanation: Indices 1 through 4 give the shortest block holding b, d, e in order.
No block contains d, so the answer is empty.

hints: Scan s1 forward to find where s2 finishes as a subsequence, then walk backwards to find the earliest start of that match.
Keep the best (shortest, then earliest) window across all forward matches.
This two-pointer pass runs in O(n * m) worst case but only O(1) extra memory.
